case.summary: Customer C11663 reported unauthorized activity on card C11663-K1, referencing transaction 3660153. Investigation revealed a series of seven unauthorized online product-C transactions between January 22 and January 31, 2017, totaling $8,551.47 and escalating to four identical charges of $1,800.00. The legitimate cardholder conducted concurrent in-person purchases in regions 327 and 315, confirming the physical card remained in their possession while card credentials were breached. Furthermore, 20 other cards across distinct accounts exhibited identical batch transaction activity with sequential transaction IDs during the same period. The activity was confirmed as card-not-present fraud, and card blocking and regulatory reporting were executed.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details a coordinated card-not-present fraud scheme involving customer C11663 and card C11663-K1. Between January 22, 2017, and January 31, 2017, seven unauthorized online product-C transactions totaling $8,551.47 were processed against card C11663-K1 across regions 327 and 315. Transaction amounts rapidly escalated from $181.73 to four consecutive charges of $1,800.00 (transactions 3660150, 3660151, 3660152, and 3660153). No device telemetry was provided for the online transactions, which were executed using an associated email on yahoo.com. During this fraudulent run, the cardholder maintained continuous physical possession of the card, evidenced by normal in-person retail purchases on January 26 (transaction 3652065 in region 327) and January 27, 2017 (transaction 3652063 in region 315). Network peer analysis identified 20 additional compromised cards from unrelated customers subjected to identical transaction patterns during January 2017. These authorizations occurred in sequential transaction ID blocks, with card C11663-K1 transactions (3660147 through 3660153) framed directly between batches for cards C07847-K1 (transactions 3660143 through 3660146) and C08943-K2 (transactions 3660155 through 3660158). The sequential execution across multiple accounts indicates automated, batch card-not-present fraud resulting from a common card data compromise. Upon confirmation of unauthorized use following customer dispute HHF-003, card C11663-K1 was permanently blocked to mitigate ongoing exposure.

answer.stop_reason: The investigation ended under policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.953, supported by two decisive independent lines of evidence: concurrent physical card usage by the holder during the unauthorized online run and tightly sequential cross-card scheme peer patterns across 20 other cards.

passages.text: Section 3b. The next best action can change. Recommend what the evidence supports now, then request more evidence if the policy calls for it, then recommend again. passages.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
passages.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

report.summary: Customer C11663 reported unauthorized activity on card C11663-K1, referencing transaction 3660153. Investigation revealed a series of seven unauthorized online product-C transactions between January 22 and January 31, 2017, totaling $8,551.47 and escalating to four identical charges of $1,800.00. The legitimate cardholder conducted concurrent in-person purchases in regions 327 and 315, confirming the physical card remained in their possession while card credentials were breached. Furthermore, 20 other cards across distinct accounts exhibited identical batch transaction activity with sequential transaction IDs during the same period. The activity was confirmed as card-not-present fraud, and card blocking and regulatory reporting were executed.
report.stop_reason: The investigation ended under policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.953, supported by two decisive independent lines of evidence: concurrent physical card usage by the holder during the unauthorized online run and tightly sequential cross-card scheme peer patterns across 20 other cards.
report.sar_narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details a coordinated card-not-present fraud scheme involving customer C11663 and card C11663-K1. Between January 22, 2017, and January 31, 2017, seven unauthorized online product-C transactions totaling $8,551.47 were processed against card C11663-K1 across regions 327 and 315. Transaction amounts rapidly escalated from $181.73 to four consecutive charges of $1,800.00 (transactions 3660150, 3660151, 3660152, and 3660153). No device telemetry was provided for the online transactions, which were executed using an associated email on yahoo.com. During this fraudulent run, the cardholder maintained continuous physical possession of the card, evidenced by normal in-person retail purchases on January 26 (transaction 3652065 in region 327) and January 27, 2017 (transaction 3652063 in region 315). Network peer analysis identified 20 additional compromised cards from unrelated customers subjected to identical transaction patterns during January 2017. These authorizations occurred in sequential transaction ID blocks, with card C11663-K1 transactions (3660147 through 3660153) framed directly between batches for cards C07847-K1 (transactions 3660143 through 3660146) and C08943-K2 (transactions 3660155 through 3660158). The sequential execution across multiple accounts indicates automated, batch card-not-present fraud resulting from a common card data compromise. Upon confirmation of unauthorized use following customer dispute HHF-003, card C11663-K1 was permanently blocked to mitigate ongoing exposure.
